messages:
elaine-cs: HarborView reporting multiple p99 spikes on embeddings API since 09:20 UTC. Customer says UX timeouts; they see spikes tied to large bulk-import jobs. Observed p95 ~ 120ms but p99 jumps to 4.2s for tenant harborview-prod. Request from CS: can we throttle other noisy tenants or provide a temporary allowlist/reservation?

mikhail-sre: pinging eng-sre. Do we have traces for the affected request IDs? any evidence of queue build-up or retries?

elaine-cs: I attached a couple of sample req IDs from the customer (they pasted them into the ticket): `req_20260315_09a1`, `req_20260315_09b7`, `req_20260315_09c3`. They said the pattern is during their nightly ingest window — lots of 1MB inputs in a single request.

jessica-obs: looking at traces now. Quick view: worker queue depth for that node pool spikes ~3x at 09:20-09:35 and CPU stays high. KV cache hit ratio drops during the window. Found tail latencies correlate with a handful of long-running batched requests from a small set of client IPs.

omar-platform: could be noisy neighbor from large batch requests — embeddings pipeline serializes some steps and holds worker slots. Do we have per-tenant concurrency limits applied? I think harborview is on the default plan with burst quota but no reserved capacity.

ryan-eng: we ship an immediate mitigation we sometimes use: apply a soft per-tenant concurrency cap + short token-bucket rate limit at the gateway for that tenant to smooth the burst. That usually knocks down p99 quickly while we investigate.

elaine-cs: Customer is asking for an allowlist-based exemption so their API keys don't get rate limited while they push. They want either a temporary per-tenant reservation for tonight or an allowlist of their ingestion IPs.

harborview-support: Confirming from HarborView — their ops team can provide a small set of CIDRs (3 IPs) for tonight if that helps. They prefer not to slow ingestion; they'd accept a temporary reserved slot if available.

mikhail-sre: short-term options: 1) Add harborview IPs to allowlist (bypass gateway rate-limiter) — risky because will let bursts through and could worsen queue; 2) Provision small reserved capacity pool for harborview (can do quickly in Dedicated if they have a commit); 3) Apply soft concurrency cap on others or increase autoscaling aggressiveness for the pool. My recommendation: do (3) + temporal reservation of ~4 extra worker slots for 2 hours if ops can stand it.

jessica-obs: additional data: here's a sample query from logs (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Content-Length: 1024000
x-tenant-id: harborview-prod
body: [..large array..]
```
Trace snippet: `latency: 4207ms, worker_queue_ms: 2300, compute_ms: 1800`

omar-platform: if we go with temporary reservation I can spin up 4 extra instances in the pool and pin them to harborview code path. Need a quick thumbs-up from eng-sre and a deploy-bot approval for capacity change.

deploy-bot: requested scale-up: 4 workers to pool-ml-eu-west.ETA ~ 6 minutes. Approval required from @mikhail-sre.

mikhail-sre: approved. Go ahead. Also enable gateway soft-throttle for other tenants with heavy concurrent requests to minimize cross-tenant noise.

omar-platform: scaling issued, will route new workers to harborview tag and add a temporary per-tenant reservation of 4 slots. I will also drop a short-lived rate-limit rule: `limit: 300 req/min for non-harborview` on the pool.

elaine-cs: letting customer know: we will reserve capacity and apply smoothing limits on others; will follow up after the ingestion window. HarborView agreed to give IPs just in case.

harborview-support: thanks, we appreciate the quick responses. We'll monitor from our side and share telemetry.

jessica-obs: after scale-up p99 dropped back to ~350ms within ~90s of new workers joining. Queue depth normalized. I’ll keep a trace watch for the next 2 hours and capture any anomalies.

ryan-eng: follow-ups: (a) evaluate adding a long-term per-tenant burst policy for large embeds (b) consider prefix-level caching improvements to avoid recompute for repeated chunks (c) document runbook for CS to request temporary reservations.

mikhail-sre: filing a short post-incident note and action items. tagging @omar-platform and @jessica-obs for follow-through. Closing thread when CS confirms customer's UX stable. :white_check_mark:
